Honestly, I’m not really sure why I’m here. My ex-husband convinced me to come, said I haven’t been myself in nearly a year. It’s hard to even pinpoint when things started feeling… off. Most days, I just feel this emptiness, like all the joy has been sucked out of everything. Even closing a big deal, something I used to live for, just feels flat now. Sometimes, these thoughts pop into my head, really disturbing ones, you know, like the urge to just… step in front of a bus or jump off a balcony, even though I don't really want to die.

Lately, though, it’s been different. I’ll go from feeling absolutely on top of the world, like I could sell ice to an Eskimo, to suddenly bursting into tears over nothing. I’ve been trying to get so much done, juggling five listings at once, redesigning my whole marketing strategy, even impulse-buying a new car. But I can't quite finish anything, always jumping from one idea to the next. And then there are the things I see. They’re usually quick, just flashes, like people standing in the corner of my eye when no one’s there, or shadows moving. It's unsettling. It gets even weirder sometimes, like I'll be listening to the radio and the lyrics just seem to be talking directly to me, giving me messages. Or I’ll find myself talking in rhymes, or words that sound similar, but don't really make sense together. It makes it hard to focus, both on clients and just, well, life.
D006-D005_h001.question_a:
"I'm really struggling, doctor. It's been about ten months since things really took a turn. I'd be flying high, feeling like I could sell every house in the county, talking a mile a minute, bouncing between calls, drawing up contracts, reorganizing the files, then suddenly wanting to redecorate my entire house – 'decorate, ornate, make it great,' I'd think. But then my mood would just crash, and I'd feel nothing, just an emptiness where joy used to be. Sometimes I get these awful thoughts, fleeting urges to just… step into traffic, even though I know I shouldn't.

But the really scary stuff started about eight months ago, while all this manic energy and crushing sadness was still going on. I started seeing things, like shimmering figures at the edge of my vision, people waving at me from empty parking lots. And the TV… it feels like the newscasters are sending me coded messages, just for me, through their expressions. I know it sounds crazy, but it feels so real.

What's really been rough is that these strange visions and those secret messages, they're not just happening when I'm feeling intensely high or low. For the past couple of weeks, I’ve been feeling relatively stable mood-wise, not those extreme ups and downs, but those visual hallucinations and that feeling of being communicated with directly have still been there, lingering even without the mood swings. It’s definitely been longer than a few weeks that I've been dealing with the mania predominantly, it's just that these other things have been constant too, regardless of how high or low my mood was at the time."

I’d start drafting a ton of listing agreements, then suddenly move to remodeling ideas for a client, then jump to redesigning my own website – couldn't finish a thing.

Then, around eight months ago, the visions started. I see people, shadowy figures mostly, just out of the corner of my eye. Sometimes they’re in my peripheral vision, and other times they just pop up in my living room. And the TV, the news anchors, they’re talking right to me, sending me secret messages through their gestures. My thoughts get so jumbled sometimes, I start rhyming words without meaning to, like "key and glee and set me free."

The past three months, though, have been the worst. All that manic energy completely drained away. Nothing brings me joy anymore. My biggest fear is driving, I keep having these sudden, terrifying urges to just swerve into oncoming traffic, or jump out of the car when I’m on a bridge. D006-D005_h002.question_a:

I try to get things done, but then my mind just flits from one thing to another, never really settling. One minute I'm on top of the world, feeling like I can solve every case, and the next I want to smash something. My squad car feels too small, my uniform too tight.

And then, things started getting really weird about eight months ago. I’d be on patrol, and it felt like bugs were crawling on my skin, or someone was messing with my hair. I’d swat at nothing, and the guys would look at me funny. Sometimes when I try to explain it, the words just… they don’t come out right. It’s like my thoughts get all jumbled and then what I say is just a mess, a word salad. It's like I know what I want to say about the world ending, about a great flood coming, but then I hear the whispers and the buzzing and I just lose it.

In the midst of all this, I went through a really dark patch, about three months ago. I just couldn’t bring myself to do anything. Getting out of bed felt impossible, and I just wanted it all to stop. I… I tried to end it then. And what’s really odd, is that even when I was at my absolute lowest, convinced the world was collapsing in on itself, those crawling sensations, those mixed-up words, they were still there, clear as day, for at least a couple of weeks, even without the intense mood swings. But these periods where my mood is just wild, cycling from high to low and back again, that restlessness, that’s actually been the majority of the time I’ve been feeling off.

I'm glad to finally be here. It’s been… a really long year and some change. For the past eleven months, I've had this incredible energy, like my mind is just racing with ideas for scripts and stories. I'm juggling so many projects at once, often starting three or four things in a day, which is great for my work as a writer, but none of them ever really get finished. Sleep? Who needs it? I’ve gone days on just a few hours, feeling totally fine, even energized. It's like I'm wired differently.

But then, for the past five months, things have shifted dramatically. Now, I feel so incredibly numb. It’s like all my emotions have just… flatlined. I can't feel joy, sadness, nothing. It’s a terrifying emptiness. And I can’t shake this crushing guilt, this absolute certainty that I’m to blame for every bad thing that happens around me, even things I logically know I couldn't control.

And throughout all of this, for over a year now, I've been feeling things. Sometimes, it’s like my skin is crawling, or tiny insects are just skittering over my arms. I keep brushing them off, but there’s nothing there. And the thoughts… I know it sounds strange, but I’m convinced there’s something horribly wrong inside of me, in my organs. My train of thought often jumps around too, from one idea to a completely unrelated one, like my brain can't stay on one track. It’s exhausting, and it’s making it impossible to focus on my writing.
D006-D005_h015.question_a:
It’s hard to pinpoint when things really started, but I’ve felt off for well over a year now, maybe around 14 months, and parts of it have been a whirlwind. For about eleven of those months, I've had this incredible energy, like I’m brimming with ideas for my writing. I’ll start a new script, then jump to a blog post, then a short story, bouncing between them all night. Sleep? Who needs it? I’ve gone days without it and felt perfectly fine, even euphoric. It’s like my mind just won't stop, and honestly, it feels amazing.

But then there are these other sensations, these disturbing thoughts... a few times now, for weeks at a time, sometimes when I'm still buzzing with that creative energy and sometimes not, I get these tingling feelings, like bugs crawling under my skin. And I have this absolute conviction that something is seriously wrong with my brain, that it's physically decaying, even though doctors say I'm fine. Those feelings, the crawling and the brain decay, have been with me for the entire fourteen months, even during the periods when I don't feel "up." In fact, for a good two weeks straight recently, I was completely convinced about my brain without feeling either high or low.

Then, there are these crashes. For about five months, it’s like a total shutdown. I feel utterly numb, like the volume on all my emotions has been turned down to zero. And the guilt… it’s overwhelming. I feel personally responsible for everything bad that happens around me, like the news reports or even just a friend having a bad day, even though I logically know it’s ridiculous. It all makes it impossible to focus on anything, whether it’s writing or even just meeting friends. The "highs" have really dominated most of this time, though – they’ve been the most consistent part of my life over the past year.

Like my emotions have been turned off. And this crushing guilt, this irrational belief that I’m somehow responsible for every bad thing that happens, it's just taken over. D006-D005_h024.question_both:
It’s hard to pinpoint when things really started going off the rails, but I’d say it's been a tough year, maybe longer. I just… I don’t feel like myself. There have been times, for a good year now, where I feel like I'm on top of the world. My mood is just unbelievably high, like I could conquer anything. During those periods, I feel like I don't need sleep at all – I’ll pull all-nighters operating or studying, feeling completely refreshed with just a few hours. I’ve probably started five new research projects in the past few months, pushing myself harder than anyone else in my residency. I even "invested" a good chunk of my savings into this new med-tech startup, which, looking back, might have been a bit impulsive.

But then there are these other times. The past nine months have had a lot more... strangeness. I keep thinking my ex-girlfriend, Sarah, is seeing someone else, even though we broke up ages ago. I get this intensely unsettling sensation, like bugs crawling under my skin, especially when I’m alone. And when I try to talk about it, my thoughts just jump around, and I know I'm not making much sense. For the past six months, even the simplest things, like grabbing a coffee, feel utterly pointless. Nothing brings me joy. I barely eat, and when I'm asked a question, it takes me forever to formulate a response. I try to sleep, but I wake up constantly, feeling completely empty. My residency is suffering, and honestly, I’m just trying to hold it together.
D006-D005_h024.question_a:
"It's been a rough year, doc. More than a year, actually. For about the past year, I've had this incredible energy. I’d jump into multiple projects at the hospital, burning the candle at both ends, not really needing much sleep. Just a few hours, and I'd be ready to go again. I even sank a significant chunk of my savings into what I thought was a brilliant new medical tech startup—didn't really scrutinize it as much as I should have. I felt so alive, buoyant, almost euphoric, like I was on top of the world. But here's the thing, for a good nine months out of that period, while I was feeling this extreme high, things started getting really weird. I became convinced my girlfriend was seeing someone else, even though there was zero proof. And I'd feel these odd crawling sensations on my skin, like bugs, but nothing was ever there. My thoughts would just race, flying off topic whenever someone asked me a question.

But for the past six months, even while those strange thoughts and sensations were happening, it’s like everything just crashed. I feel empty, just hollow inside. My appetite is gone, I barely eat, and I wake up constantly throughout the night. It's like my brain just can’t keep up – even talking feels like wading through mud. The real kicker is that through all of this, for at least two weeks straight, a few months back, I was definitely having those weird delusions about my girlfriend and the crawling sensations, even when I wasn't feeling particularly high or low. And even with all the ups and downs, that high, energetic period, where I was taking on the world, that’s been the predominant state for most of this past year, mixed in with everything else."

My wife, bless her, noticed I was barely getting a few hours of sleep yet felt completely refreshed, ready to tackle anything. I started reaching out to old contacts, even new ones, with this overwhelming urge to connect and share my "brilliant" new ideas. I even, well, let's just say a few indiscretions happened that are quite out of character for a man my age.

And I know, deep down, that I'm meant for something bigger; I have a unique gift for understanding the universe's secrets, a talent far beyond mere writing. Sometimes when my wife asks me a direct question, I find my thoughts just drift to other, more profound topics, and I struggle to get back to what she was asking. Other times, I just can't find the words, and my speech dwindles to barely a whisper. These strange experiences, the seeing things and knowing my destiny, have been there even when I'm not feeling this intense high.

Then, for about six months recently, things swung the other way. I felt utterly hollow inside, an emptiness I can’t describe.
